Our twelve-person engineering team has drifted into a branching model that costs us more than we admit.

## The problem

Feature branches now live for two to four weeks on average, and integration has become an event rather than a habit. Merge conflicts routinely eat a full day of engineering time, and by the time a branch lands, its author has often forgotten the context that made the change safe.

- Branches older than a week correlate with our three worst production incidents this quarter, all caused by integration surprises no one caught earlier.
- Code review quality has dropped because reviewers now face 800-line diffs instead of small, digestible changes.

## The proposal

I propose we move to trunk-based development: every engineer commits to main at least daily, behind feature flags where work is incomplete, with CI enforcing a green trunk at all times.

- Feature flags let us ship incomplete work safely, decoupling deployment from release and letting product enable features selectively.
- A green-trunk policy, enforced by CI, removes the "integration day" scramble by ensuring nobody merges on top of a broken build.
- Smaller, daily commits shorten lead time and make code review useful again, since reviewers can reason about a diff in minutes, not hours.

This is not radical; it is standard practice at most high-performing engineering organizations, and our CI pipeline already supports it.

## What could go wrong

The strongest objection is real: without long-lived branches, half-finished work risks leaking into production, and feature flags add complexity and cleanup debt if poorly managed. This is a legitimate cost, not a hypothetical one; teams that adopt trunk-based development without flag discipline end up with tangled conditionals and forgotten flags littering the codebase.

We can mitigate this with a flag registry, a mandatory expiration date on every flag, and a two-week pilot on one team before a full rollout. That is a real cost worth paying deliberately, not a reason to keep merging in the dark for weeks.

I would like a decision by the end of next week.
